evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A03612-001, Shuowen quotations and later variant history
evidence.text: The entry quotes Shuowen as separate entries: 号 is a painful cry, formed from 口 above 丂; 號 means ‘to call’ and is formed from 号 and 虎. It reports that later lexicons mixed the graphs and readings, with 号 used for 號. This is a record of the dictionary tradition, not independent proof of either graph’s original construction.
evidence.title: [A03612] 號 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry gives 丂 as kǎo and quotes Shuowen’s explanation of breath wishing to emerge but obstructed above. This supports 丂’s traditional independent account; it does not establish 丂 as the phonetic element of 号.
evidence.title: [C00001] 丂 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The official record gives current Mandarin kǎo for 丂 (U+4E02). This is modern reading metadata, not evidence of an ancient sound role in 号.
evidence.title: Unihan data for U+4E02

evidence.text: The official record gives current Mandarin hào for 号 (U+53F7). It also lists 號 as a semantic variant and traditional variant. These are current database properties, not evidence about ancient graph formation.
evidence.title: Unihan data for U+53F7

evidence.text: The official record gives current Mandarin hào for 號 (U+865F), lists hào and háo among its Hanyu Pinyin readings, and identifies 号 as its simplified variant. The single kMandarin value is current metadata, not an account of historical sound change.
evidence.title: Unihan data for U+865F

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction, version 1.1
evidence.field: Old Chinese reconstruction table, GSR 1041 series
evidence.text: In the authors’ 2014 published table, 丂 is kǎo, MC khawX, OC *C.qʰˤuʔ (marked ‘Shuōwén; no pre-Qín exx.’); 号 is hào, MC hawH, OC *[g]ˤaw-s; 號 is háo, MC haw, OC *[C.g]ˤaw and MC hawH, OC *Cə.[g]ˤaw-s. This supports a sound comparison between 号 and 號 within the named system but not between 丂 and 号. The local TSV supplied in the input differs in notation for 丂 and 号, including a rounded-vowel symbol and bracket detail; the two transcriptions should remain attributed to their respective sources.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction, version 1.1
evidence.field: Old Chinese reconstruction table, GSR 1041 series
evidence.text: The table gives 号: Mandarin hào, Middle Chinese hawH, Old Chinese *[g]ˤaw-s (‘command, call (n.)’); and 號: Mandarin háo, Middle Chinese haw, Old Chinese *[C.g]ˤaw (‘call out’), plus hawH and *Cə.[g]ˤaw-s (‘command, call (n.)’). In this reconstruction their sound similarity makes 号 a plausible sound element in 號. This does not make 丂 a phonetic in 号 or establish the graph’s origin.
evidence.title: BaxterSagartOCbyGSR2014-09-20

evidence.text: The entry places 号 and 號 in the same Zhengzhang phonetic series and gives 号 *ɦlaːws and 號 *ɦlaːw, *ɦlaːws. This is a secondary report of that reconstruction and makes a phonetic relation plausible within that system. The same entry’s 口+丂 semantic account does not establish 丂 as a phonetic in 号.
evidence.title: 号 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary, citing Zhengzhang Shangfang and Baxter–Sagart
evidence.field: 號 graphic analysis and phonetic-series account
evidence.text: The entry reports a proposal that 號 began as a tiger with a line for exhaled air, later adding 口 or 言, and analyzes the current 號 as 号 phonetic plus 虎 semantic. It also gives Mandarin hào/háo, Middle Chinese hawH/haw, and reconstructions attributed to Zhengzhang and Baxter–Sagart. This is a secondary proposal; the accessed evidence does not independently establish the early pictograph, a historical name for a tiger’s cry, or a whole-graph sound loan.
evidence.title: 號 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A03612, dated dictionary examples and senses
evidence.text: The entry cites examples under 號 for crying, calling, commands, summons, naming, titles, signs and assigned numbers, including examples attributed to the Book of Documents, Zuo zhuan, Zhuangzi, Shiji and Han shu. These citations establish that the dictionary associates the readings and senses with those texts; they do not date surviving witnesses or establish the first occurrence or a complete semantic sequence.
evidence.title: [A03612] 號 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A03612-001, cited lexicons and form history
evidence.text: The entry cites Yùpiān, Guǎngyùn, Lèipiān and the Dunhuang俗字譜 for overlapping spellings and readings: crying or pain, call, summon, command, and posthumous title. It states that Shuowen initially distinguishes 号 and 號, while later lexicons conflate them. This supports later graphic and lexical convergence, not a single origin for the two Shuowen head characters.
evidence.title: [A03612-001] 号 (號) - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry identifies 号 as an alternative form of 號 in its present dictionary organization and explains the visible 號 as containing 号 and 虎. This is evidence for the conventional current relationship, while the entry separately records their distinction in Shuowen.

search_audit.outcome: Opened the Ministry’s 号/號 variant record, which quotes the separate Shuowen forms, and the 號 record, which quotes semantic examples and gives cited senses. Search surfaced an oracle-bone database overview and institutional inscription database, but did not verify an exact dated 号 or 號 inscription or earliest semantic attestation.

Search did not return an inspectable page for the exact radical 157 file. Adjacent radical file pages identify their author and CC BY-SA terms, but this is not verified metadata for radical 157; no asset approved.

gaps: No original historical glyph pixels for 号 or 號 were inspected. The Commons category lists the candidate radical 157 file, but its exact page, SVG and imageinfo API were inaccessible; its identity, source and reuse terms remain unverified. Adjacent file metadata was not imputed to it.

The inspected sources quote Shuowen’s separate entry for 号 as a painful cry and 號 as calling. No independently checked oracle-bone or bronze primary record established either graph’s earliest attestation or a continuous graphic sequence; catalogue leads and search excerpts were insufficient.

The source tradition for 號’s tiger-roar proposal is secondary and does not establish an original tiger-call word or independently recoverable pronunciation for that depicted object. No whole-graph sound loan is supported.

The readings establish modern kǎo for 丂, hào for 号 and hào for 號. The published Baxter–Sagart table gives 丂 *C.qʰˤuʔ, 号 *[g]ˤaw-s and 號 *[C.g]ˤaw/*Cə.[g]ˤaw-s; local TSV notation differs for 丂 and 号, and the exact local rows are not external publications. Preserve provenance and notation separately.

The evidence documents dictionary-cited senses and later form convergence, but not the first occurrence of each sense or a fully dated pathway from cry/call through summons, title/name, command, mark/sign and number. Dates attributed to classical works are not dates of surviving witnesses.

No proposed sound component is assigned to the independent graph 号. Shuowen and the Ministry dictionary give 口+丂 with a painful-cry/breath-obstruction explanation, while 2014 Baxter–Sagart values for 丂 and 号 do not supply a persuasive phonetic match. Separately, 号 is a plausible phonetic component in 號 based on cited reconstructions.
